sentences.text: Vide this judgment, I seek to dispose off the case of the prosecution filed against the accused persons namely Ajay Nemani and Inderjeet and for having committed the offences punishable u/s 420/120 B of Indian Penal Code, 1861 (hereinafter referred as "IPC") and 20 & 25 Indian Telegraph Act.

2. In nutshell the allegations against accused persons are that they had entered into criminal conspiracy to set up illegal telephone exchange in Delhi by bypassing the official VSNL gateway whereby they caused huge revenue loss to government of India and caused security threat to nation.

It is the case of prosecution that accused persons cheated MTNL as they obtained telephone lines from it by deceiving it into believing that they would be used as per agreement however, they were unauthorizedly used for receiving international calls by bypassing the VSNL gateway and thereby caused cumulative loss of more than Rs.7.5 Crore to government.

The accused persons have also alleged to have established and maintained telephone exchange by illegally installing unauthorized equipments without licence and permission and that they mischeviously and dishonestly tempered with telegraph lines and shifted them to cabin no.35 at premise no. 707/56 Eros Apartment Nehru Place and F10 Lajpat Nagar from their designated placed.

It is alleged that this was done to receive international calls on RAGHAV SHARMA SHARMA Date:
2025.12.26 FIR No. 27/2001 State vs. Ajay Nemani & Anr Page 2 of 25 17:11:51 +0530 these lines and to distribute them amongst customers by setting up DID /
EPABX exchange with use of CAC multiplexer and other telecom equipments.
3. After registration of the case, necessary investigation was carried out by the IO concerned.
Site plan was prepared.
Statement of witnesses were recorded under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (hereinafter, "CrPC).
Relevant record was collected.
Final report under section 173 CrPC, was prepared against the abovenamed accused persons and chargesheet was presented in the court.
After taking cognizance of the offence, the accused persons were summoned to face trial.
4. A copy of chargesheet was supplied to accused in terms of section 207 of CrPC.
On finding a prima facie case against the accused persons, charge under section 420/120 B IPC, 20 & 25 Indian Telegraph Act was framed against the accused persons on 04.03.2005.
The accused persons pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.

PW12 being the IO was responsible to conduct independent and fair investigation to find out the truth of the matter and to find out real culprits if there were any.
Contrary to his duty, IO in the present case merely acted at the instance of the officers of above department, complied the documents and prepared the report without finding out whether there was concrete evidence to prove in court that accused persons were involved in the offence.
35. From the appreciation of evidence noted above, it can be stated in clear terms that the prosecution has miserably failed to prove any of its allegations against the accused pesons.
The seizure memos were prepared belatedly and they do not bear the proof of their contents.
They were false documents prepared subsequently only to make out a case against accused persons.
The entire investigation conducted by IO(s) was solely concentrated towards making a case out against accused persons rather than finding the truth of the matter.
They rather prepared the chargesheet on the basis of unfounded assumption and on the basis of baseless conjectures.
The prosecution has failed miserably to prove that accused persons had used prohibited machineries, had diverted telephone lines illegally, had received international calls on domestic numbers bypassing official channel.
There was no proof whatsoever with prosecution except for oral statement of the witnesses ascerting, without any proof, that above acts by RAGHAV RAGHAV SHARMA SHARMA Date:
2025.12.26 17:15:16 +0530 were done by accused persons.
Unfortunately, IO(s) did not do their job of investigating and finding the truth and merely relied on such assertions.
